findings:
🔵 [r5-spawn-error-swallowed] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `startWatcherDetached` attaches a no-op `child.on('error')` and returns `started` synchronously, so an async spawn failure (e.g. `nohup` or `sh` missing from PATH while `flock` is present) yields no stderr line from `set`; the realistic missing-tool case (`flock`) is caught by the foreground probe and tested (case 5), and `nohup`/`sh` are universally present, so this is hardening only. Smallest follow-up: write one stderr line in the `error` handler (it fires on nextTick, before exit) or drop `nohup` since `detached:true` + redirected stdio already makes it redundant.
🔵 [r5-suite-orphan-window] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `session-mode-watcher.test.sh` registers kill PIDs only from the published envelope; if a launch succeeds but no envelope appears within 15 s (slow host), the watcher is not in `KILL_PIDS` and survives the trap (bounded by `--idle-exit`, confined to the /dev/shm fixture live dir). Follow-up: also enumerate `count_watchers`-style `/proc` matches for `$KEY` in `cleanup_smw` and kill those by PID. Not blocking: lock-held and idle-exit bound it and nothing can reach the real store.
🔵 [r5-autostart-string-only] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The switch honours only the literal string `0`; `false`/empty are treated as enabled. Matches the spec's stated contract (`0` = never start) and lib.sh exports exactly `0`, so no in-scope failure; note for the P3 idle-supersede row if the knob grows values.
